question: Which AI agents create the most value?
html:
Which AI Agents Create the Most Value

By company, Thomas Scientific ($3.8M est.) and Frontline ($3.6M est.) agents create the most value. Together they are over half of the program's $12.7M est. run-rate. The plan does not show agent-by-agent values, so a ranking of individual agents needs the full agent list.

Value by company

All figures are EBITDA-equivalent run-rate after ramp, built on analyst assumptions (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Portfolio companyEst. annual valueRoadmap range
Thomas Scientific$3.84M est.$1.25–4.8M
Frontline$3.59M est.$1.5–4.2M
BPI$2.27M est.$0.85–3.75M
CET$1.32M est.$0.62–2.62M
Punctual Pros$0.88M est.$0.32–1.12M
Fair Harbor$0.77M est.$0.40–1.75M
  • Each total sits inside its roadmap range (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • The totals are not de-duplicated, so the $12.7M is likely overstated where agents overlap.

Value by rollout wave

  • Wave 3, revenue agents: $4.19M est. This is the largest wave.
  • Wave 2, finance agents: $3.91M est.
  • Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents: $2.81M est. This wave has the clearest baselines and lowest risk.
  • Wave 4, monitoring services: $1.77M est.

Value rises in the later waves. Confidence falls in those waves, because the baselines are weaker there.

Strongest single-agent case

The Punctual Pros missed-call and after-hours booking agent has the most worked-out model (Voice AI research).

  • It recovers about $1.37M est. a year of revenue from unanswered calls.
  • It adds about $403k est. from outbound member renewals.
  • The combined $1.78M est. is about 8.1% of Punctual Pros revenue.
  • That $1.78M is revenue. The plan's $0.88M est. for Punctual Pros is EBITDA-equivalent. The two figures should not be compared directly.

Caveats

  • Call, ticket, invoice, quote and member volumes are analyst estimates (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • Most performance metrics come from vendor case studies. They are self-reported and unaudited (Voice AI research).
  • The Punctual Pros call volume of about 3,502 a month is backed out of an estimated $22M of revenue. It is not a counted figure.
  • The missed-call share could range from 10% to 35%, so the recovered-revenue figure could move widely.

What would settle the ranking

  • Estimated value for each of the 45 agents, from the full plan.
  • System-of-record counts at each portfolio company:
  • Calls and missed calls, from telephony.
  • Tickets, from the professional services automation (PSA) system.
  • Invoices and quotes, from the ERP.
  • Members, from the customer system.
  • An overlap check, so value counted under two agents is removed.

Next actions

  1. Pull the full agent list and rank the 45 agents by estimated value. Flag any agent above $0.5M est. for early review.
  2. Replace assumed volumes with system-of-record counts at Thomas Scientific and Frontline first, since they carry most of the value.
  3. Pull three months of Punctual Pros call logs. Use them to confirm the missed-call rate before the Wave 1 launch.
  4. Run the overlap check across the agents so the portfolio total is defensible to the investment committee.
